question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{\sqrt{6}+2\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{8}{\sqrt{6}+2\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3}} & = \\ \frac{8(\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3})}{(\sqrt{6})^{2}-(2\sqrt{3})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{8(\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3})}{6-4\cdot 3} & = \\ \frac{8(\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3})}{6-12} & = \\ \frac{8(\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3})}{(-6)} & = \\ -\frac{8(\sqrt{6}-2\sqrt{3})}{6} & = \\ \frac{4(2\sqrt{3}-\sqrt{6})}{3}\end{aligned}
$$
